question.prompt: The \(64\) whole numbers from \(1\) through \(64\) are written, one per square, on a checkerboard (an \(8\) by \(8\) array of \(64\) squares). The first \(8\) numbers are written in order across the first row, the next \(8\) across the second row, and so on. After all \(64\) numbers are written, the sum of the numbers in the four corners will be

solutions.explanation:
Each row contains \(8\) numbers, so moving down one row adds \(8\) to an entry. From the first row to the eighth row there are \(7\) such moves.

The upper corners contain \(1\) and \(8\). Therefore the lower corners contain
\[
1+7\times8=57\qquad\text{and}\qquad8+7\times8=64.
\]
Pairing the corner numbers makes their sum easy to calculate:
\[
(1+64)+(8+57)=65+65=130.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{130}\), choice A.
solutions.title: Use the pattern down each column
